desc: Parse input: H, W, X, start (P,Q), and the H×W grid of strengths.
Initialize cur = S[P][Q], mark start visited, and push its up-to-4 neighbors into a min-heap (smallest strength first).
Loop: pop the smallest frontier slime; if s*X >= cur, break (no frontier slime is absorbable); otherwise absorb (cur += s) and push its unvisited neighbors.

Justify greedy correctness: absorbing only increases cur and grows the frontier, so absorbing everything absorbable is optimal; min-heap check is valid since if the smallest frontier slime fails the threshold, all do.
Handle edge cases: strict inequality (X=1 absorbs nothing unless strictly smaller), 1x1 grid, Python big ints avoid overflow (s*X up to 1e21).
Write final code with fast I/O (sys.stdin.buffer.read), 0-indexed grid, visited marked at push time, and print cur; logic sanity-checked against the three samples (28 / 5 / 1343).
